# Shared usage tooling implementation plan

## Authority and readiness

This task-scoped plan implements [the approved scope and architecture](usage-tooling.md), supporting CAP-05/NFR-006/NFR-007 and CAP-04/NFR-008. [Planning gates](planning-gates.md#shared-usage-tooling) owns disposition. Agent planning readiness, 2026-11-17: the ordered design below is ready for implementation after exact-candidate documentation QA/reconciliation. This is agent authorization, not human approval or executed acceptance. Product/catalog implementation, actual-history refresh, actual contributions/tracker publication and published protocol changes remain excluded. No additional human plan or release approval is required.

The maintenance package MUST remain separate from the future catalog package: project `dscat-usage`, import package `dscat_usage`, version `0.1.0`, Python `>=3.14`, stdlib runtime plus Git. Source MUST live in `tools/usage/src/dscat_usage`; packaging MUST live in `tools/usage/pyproject.toml`. This does not change the catalog's version, Typer/Pydantic boundary or approved product plan. Release tags MUST use `usage-v0.1.0` and subsequent compatible tooling versions, avoiding catalog release claims. No public Python API is promised.

## Frozen command contract

Both `python -m dscat_usage` and installed `dscat-usage` MUST expose the same commands. All commands except `--help`/`--version` MUST take explicit `--state PATH`; commands consuming configuration MUST take `--config PATH`. No default history discovery or network target is permitted. Human diagnostics MUST use bounded generic reasons; `--json` MUST emit a strict schema-v1 status object with `schema`, `status`, `counts`, `candidate_digest` and `remote_commit` (unavailable values null). It MUST NOT emit source identities or paths. Help MUST show the proprietary notice.

| Command/options in addition to state/config | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `setup --secret-file PATH` | Create private contributor/config/templates without replacing existing files; validate an externally provisioned 32-byte secret. Config MUST be explicit thereafter. |
| `map --entry PATH` | Validate a private schema-v1 mapping entry and locked atomic upsert; conflicting primary attribution MUST fail. Entry dimensions/precedence follow the specification. |
| `migrate --snapshot PATH --phase-map PATH --registry PATH [--identity-map PATH]` | Explicitly validate supported legacy snapshot/map inputs and copy into separate locked private state; optional private identity associations permit only uniquely verified native-identity promotion. Preserve legacy inputs/pointers; no refresh or Git transport. Unsupported/unsafe inputs fail `3`, attribution/identity conflicts fail `4`, lock contention fails `7`; unmatched identities remain historical/nonadditive with unavailable coverage. |
| `refresh` | Read only configured histories, freeze private source-prefix/SQLite observations and produce the next validated contribution. No Git transport. |
| `contribute --remote TARGET --branch NAME --generator-invocation ID` | Fetch, merge this computer's frozen contribution, render and freeze complete candidate; always stop for review. No push. |
| `check [--candidate DIGEST]` | Read-only revalidation of frozen inputs, ledger, complete outgoing tree and review bindings, if supplied. MUST NOT refresh, fetch or repair state. |
| `review --attestation PATH --execution-evidence PATH` | Validate externally supplied procedural fresh-review evidence and freeze its digest with attestation; MUST NOT author PASS evidence. |
| `update --remote TARGET --branch NAME --generator-invocation ID` | Without a candidate, prepare as contribute; with a frozen reviewed candidate, revalidate and ordinary-push without refresh. Stale parent MUST preserve old candidate, fetch/remerge/regenerate and require new review. |
| `readback --remote TARGET --branch NAME --expected-commit HEX --reader-invocation ID` | Separate fresh-execution clone validation of exact commit/ancestry, ledger, projections and generic metadata; record remote verification separately. |

Config MUST contain schema version, explicit source root/project selector, private map/rates/vocabulary paths, secret-file path and resource limits; these paths MUST remain private. Remote target MUST be supplied explicitly at preparation/resume and match frozen bindings. State MUST NOT be nested in a transport checkout. A local bare remote MUST work without a service. Actual publication remains outside this task pending the separate protocol transition.

Exit codes MUST be stable: `0` successful operation (including confirmed submission, separately from readback); `2` invalid arguments/schema/config; `3` missing/inaccessible/unsupported source or unsafe/corrupt state; `4` identity/domain/generation/measurement/mapping conflict; `5` independent review required, absent or stale; `6` transport failure or unresolved remote identity; `7` lock contention/recovery required. Review-required preparation MUST return `5` even when candidate creation succeeded. Error paths MUST preserve previous accepted pointers. JSON output MUST distinguish `prepared`, `review_required`, `submitted`, `remote_verified`, `unavailable`, `conflict` and `failed`; no submitted status implies fresh independent readback.

## Interfaces and schema ownership

U1 MUST freeze strict schema-v1 constructors/validators and typed dataclasses in `schema.py`; later increments MUST reuse them. Canonical JSON MUST use sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8 and reject duplicate keys/nonfinite numbers. Every boundary MUST reject unknown keys, bool-as-int, unbounded strings/numbers, unsupported versions and invalid token subsets. HMAC tuples and domain marker MUST follow the architecture exactly. Defaults MUST limit each source file to 64 MiB, captured total to 512 MiB, records to 1,000,000 and generic diagnostic entries to 100; larger inputs MUST fail unavailable without replacing accepted state. Configurable limits MUST remain positive and bounded by these hard maxima.

| Interface/artifact | Owner and contract |
| --- | --- |
| `private.py`: `StateStore`, `atomic_write`, `locked`; private `manifest.json`, `map.json`, snapshots and pointers | U1; mode 0700 directories/0600 files where supported, exclusive owner lock, fsync/atomic replacement, symlink/path rejection, no automatic stale-lock deletion. Recovery MUST verify inactive owner. |
| `importer.py`: `capture`; `identity.py`: `receipt`; `mapping.py`: `resolve`; `migration.py`: `migrate` | U1; read-only supported native JSONL and SQLite history adapters, stable prefix capture/read-only transactions; private normalized records and digests. Unknown schema/identity MUST fail affected contribution. No hash-of-content identity fallback. Migration MUST implement the specification compatibility contract with validated legacy layouts, private historical archive and explicitly verified identity associations. |
| `schema.py`: `Contribution`, `Observation`, `Ledger`, `Candidate`, `ReviewEvidence`, `Attestation`, `Status` | U1; private raw associations MUST be structurally separate from transport observations. Strict validators for all later boundaries MUST exist before use. |
| `ledger.py`: `merge`; transport `usage-ledger.json` | U2; full latest observations keyed by contributor/generation/predecessor, exact receipt dedup, compatible enrichment only, conflicts quarantined privately and blocking. Explicit correction/removal MUST be represented and reviewed; unavailable input MUST NOT create replacement. |
| `metrics.py`: `aggregate`, `price`; `render.py`: `render` | U2; single canonical corpus, independent dimension precedence, global interval unions, Decimal dated/list counterfactual costs, strict public allowlist. Owned projection files MUST be `Usage.md`, `Usage-by-RTM.md`, `Usage-by-Task.md`, `Usage-Models.md`, `Usage-Methodology.md`, `Usage-Evidence.md`; other files MUST remain byte-identical. |
| `candidate.py`: `prepare`, `validate`; `review.py`: `validate_review`; `transport.py`: `submit`, `readback` | U3; private immutable candidate directory, tree/input/parent/generation/domain/schema/invocation/metadata bindings, ordinary push and remote identity confirmation, independent clone validation. |
| `cli.py`: `main`, package `__main__.py`; templates, user instructions and wheel/sdist | U4; command contract, clean install/offline walkthrough and release identity evidence. |

Transport observations MUST carry only the specification's allowed identity/framing/facts; generic metadata MUST use fixed neutral commit subject and explicit generic author identity. Private config MUST load exact reviewed model/provider/effort/tier vocabulary, public RTM inventory and opaque registered labels; missing vocabularies MUST produce unknown/unallocated, never free-form transport. Pricing templates MUST be empty by default; unknown prices remain unpriced. U1 MUST freeze sanitized synthetic compatibility fixtures for the existing schema-v1 snapshot/registry and phase-map layouts, including their private identity-association schema; no fixture MAY copy actual state. Migration input digests and private provenance MUST remain private. Canonical serialized schema fixtures MUST be frozen by U1 and expanded compatibly by U2/U3, with all changes reverified.

Review evidence MUST contain schema, opaque task ID, generator/reviewer invocation IDs, complete-candidate scope, PASS/FAIL disposition, candidate/tree/input/metadata/parent digests and evidence timestamp. Attestation MUST repeat exact bindings and reference execution-evidence digest. Both MUST be private and strictly validated; same invocation, wrong scope, absent/mismatched binding, changed candidate or evidence predating candidate creation MUST fail. A coordinator MUST provide real fresh-dispatch/return evidence and retain its provenance privately. This validator checks supported procedural bindings; it cannot authenticate reviewer honesty or independence against a process controlling private state. Synthetic evidence MUST be marked synthetic and accepted only for disposable local-remote test configurations. Production paths MUST consume real supplied evidence without placeholder hooks that reject every valid review.

## Ordered increments and acceptance inventory

Every increment MUST use a fresh implementation agent followed by a different fresh verifier. No agent MUST verify its own implementation. All files within an increment MUST have one writer; dependent/shared schemas, CLI and task/RTM writes MUST be serialized. Parallel pure U2 metrics/render work MAY be assigned disjoint files only after U1 schema fixtures are frozen; each implementation invocation and verifier MUST remain distinct. A fresh independent security/privacy review MUST cover the combined U1–U4 candidate before integration; no waiver is assumed.

| Increment/dependency | Ownership and requirements | Verification inventory |
| --- | --- | --- |
| U1 private capture foundation; none | `schema.py`, `private.py`, `identity.py`, `mapping.py`, `importer.py`, `migration.py`; unit tests for these only. A1/A2/A4/A7/A8; NFR-006/007/008 | Empty/missing/denied inputs; SQLite read-only transaction and schema variants; JSONL prefix/partial line; stable native IDs and copied sources; domain mismatch; map precedence/conflict; simultaneous writers/killed writer; malicious paths/symlinks/corrupt manifests; unknown labels/keys/nonfinite/limits; supported legacy snapshot/phase-map/registry migration, replay, byte-preserved legacy inputs and pointers, explicit attribution precedence, inferred/unmapped/unknown/open preservation, missing native histories, ambiguous/truncated identity rejection, unsupported schemas/corrupt hashes/conflicting maps, lock/failure preservation and no Git/refresh side effects. Sanitized adapter code MAY be adapted from ignored local tools but MUST remove legacy weak identity/defaults/inference. |
| U2 validated merge and projection; U1 pass | `ledger.py`, `metrics.py`, `render.py`; synthetic ledger/measurement tests. A3/A4/A7/A8; NFR-006/007/008 | Disjoint computers; identical replay; new generation/replacement/removal; same-generation fork/rollback/lost predecessor; copied overlaps; non-null conflicts persisting across contributors; unknown enrichment/open closure; no-response turns; global/category unions; cache/reasoning subsets; missing tokens/prices; dated vs current rates and separate currencies; complete projection/transport allowlist. |
| U3 frozen review/transport; U1/U2 pass | `candidate.py`, `review.py`, `transport.py`; disposable Git integration tests. A3/A5/A6/A8; NFR-006/007/008 | Complete unchanged-tree review; absent/same/stale/tampered evidence and metadata; disjoint/simultaneous contributors; stale-parent remerge/new review; unrelated-page preservation; rejected push; ambiguous successful push plus identity readback; unresolved remote leaves pointer unchanged; fresh clone validation; mutation immediately before submit; force push never invoked. |
| U4 executable distribution; U1–U3 pass | `cli.py`, package entry points, `tools/usage/pyproject.toml`, templates, `tools/usage/README.md`, package tests/walkthrough; task/RTM updates serialized. A1–A8; NFR-006/007/008 | Every command/option/exit/status; fresh-clone setup, real supported native-format synthetic source ingestion, two private states sharing provisioned synthetic secret, contribution/review/resume/readback; explicit legacy-format synthetic migration with and without verified identity association and preserved old-tool inputs; negative recovery; wheel/sdist clean install outside checkout; help/version/proprietary license/offline execution. No private source/tool dependency. |

Each verifier MUST run the bounded tests and previous-increment regression suite against exact source and dirty-file digests, inspect negative preservation/recovery and record behavior evidence. Target MUST be 100% statement/branch coverage with only narrow documented engineering-policy exceptions; no acceptance/security behavior may be waived. U4 MUST supply a runnable `python -m unittest discover -s tools/usage/tests -v` and `python tools/usage/tests/walkthrough.py` using only temporary synthetic sources/states/remotes. Until U4 those planned commands MUST NOT be reported as existing or passing.

## Local acceptance and tooling release

U4 MUST freeze eligible pinned build/lint/type/test tools with 14-day exclusion and hashes in a tooling-only uv lock without adding runtime dependencies. Applicable Ruff ALL, formatter and ty error-level checks MUST pass with narrow documented conflict exclusions. Verification MUST run `uv run --project tools/usage --frozen ruff check tools/usage`, `uv run --project tools/usage --frozen ruff format --check tools/usage`, `uv run --project tools/usage --frozen ty check tools/usage/src`, unit/branch coverage and the synthetic walkthrough. Exact supported flags/tool versions MUST be checked during implementation and any necessary compatible correction recorded before claiming success.

The walkthrough MUST create two separate temporary source/state roots and one local bare Git remote, seed an unrelated page, provision one synthetic secret outside Git, ingest native-format synthetic histories, migrate a synthetic legacy snapshot/maps into separate state and verify legacy byte preservation plus unknown/nonadditive handling, map opaque synthetic dispatches, prepare/review/push/readback both contributors, retry copied overlap, close an open turn, and prove stale review and conflict failures preserve accepted state. It MUST print expected aggregate/commit identities without private paths/IDs and clean up temporary data. The review fixture MUST explicitly describe its synthetic-only scope. Real review requires coordinator evidence from fresh execution; the walkthrough MUST NOT claim actual independent review occurred.

Fresh local acceptance MUST build `dscat_usage-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl` and `dscat_usage-0.1.0.tar.gz` from the tooling project, inspect archives for secret/private data and source inclusion, install wheel and rebuild/install sdist in clean environments outside the checkout, and execute the same walkthrough without history/tracker/network access. Source distribution MUST include package tests, empty templates, instructions, license and approved maintenance plan/spec evidence, without packaging private state or catalog runtime claims. The implementation MUST preserve the root catalog pyproject and unrelated documents.

The tooling release MUST include original locally verified wheel/sdist, SHA256SUMS, source-commit/artifact manifest, a truthful tooling/runtime SBOM (stdlib/Git external prerequisite; no invented Python runtime dependencies), build/dev inventory, neutral notes and concise test/security/install evidence. Fresh advisory/exploitation/licensing applicability checks MUST cover actual build/dev dependencies and relevant prerequisites; unavailable/unknown status MUST remain explicit and block applicable readiness. Catalog schema/Excel/accessibility/product-release scenarios do not apply to this tooling-only artifact. [Delivery policy](governance.md#local-verification-and-distribution) and repository protection/PR policy apply; the catalog [delivery plan](delivery-plan.md) does not authorize or block unrelated catalog implementation here.

Integration MUST use protected PR/rebase flow, verify remote-main identities, then a fresh release agent MUST record DEC-045 standing delegation with exact main/artifact hashes and publish those same bytes. A separate fresh post-release agent MUST download `usage-v0.1.0` assets, verify hashes/version, install both downloaded artifacts in clean environments and run the synthetic/offline walkthrough plus released-source documentation checks. No actual wiki protocol migration/publication or private-history execution is authorized. Failure MUST keep the task incomplete and follow ordinary correction/new-version release policy; no silent asset replacement.

## Documentation evidence and next gate

Repository-wide structural checks and full bounded fresh semantic review/reconciliation MUST cover the combined exact candidate before implementation. Suggested partitions: (1) usage specification/plan/task plus RTM supporting rows; (2) authority/governance/gates/workflow/phase records; (3) unchanged product requirements/architecture/intake/model/research; (4) unchanged implementation/dependency/verification/delivery/security/repository policy and remaining task/entry documents. The coordinator MUST inventory every maintained document, assign every applicable semantic-matrix area and obtain a distinct reconciliation reviewer. Identical unchanged content/applicability MAY reuse exact previously retained review evidence; changed documents/dependencies MUST receive fresh coverage. This suggestion is not a claimed completed coverage ledger.

[The task stage ledger](tasks/usage-tooling.md#stage-ledger) owns actual implementation, test, packaging, independent review, integration and release status; this plan defines their execution contracts. A failed scope/security/compatibility decision MUST return to the earliest affected readiness gate; routine implementation choices within these contracts remain autonomous.

# Shared usage tooling

## Scope and authority

This maintenance specification supports CAP-05/NFR-006/NFR-007 and CAP-04/NFR-008. The human approved the exact requirements decision package with SHA-256 `172c6139fde399335a83e62fe048d0d18b5ff2ef85cad2025cb3ab3deaf1ff43` on 2026-11-17. That package remains private; this sanitized specification records its operative scope. [Planning gates](planning-gates.md#shared-usage-tooling) owns disposition. Existing approved product requirements MUST remain unchanged.

Deliverables MUST comprise reusable tracked core tooling, synthetic tests, empty templates and setup/use instructions. Raw histories, private attribution/configuration/state, credentials, source paths and original identifiers MUST remain outside Git. Existing ignored tooling/maps MUST NOT be overwritten. Actual-history refresh, actual contributions, tracker publication and publication of the wiki protocol revision are excluded. Synthetic local Git end-to-end testing, tooling PR integration and tooling release/download verification are included.

## Acceptance

These task acceptance labels refine the existing supporting requirements; they are not new product requirement IDs.

| Anchor | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | Fresh-clone setup MUST run without private code from another computer, create private state without destructive replacement and report inaccessible/missing history/configuration as unavailable rather than complete/zero. Explicit supported private snapshot/map migration MUST preserve legacy inputs and supported attribution without guessing; unsupported/ambiguous inputs MUST refuse promotion and leave unknown history explicit. |
| A2 | Each computer MUST prepare and submit its own contribution without central map editing. Local map writes MUST lock and atomically preserve other writers; conflicting primary attribution MUST fail. |
| A3 | Submissions MUST preserve other contributors, be idempotent, and replace prior contributor observations by stable record identity. State and identity MUST remain independent of checkout path and hostname. |
| A4 | Shared/copied histories MUST count once. Conflicting observations MUST be quarantined and block affected merge; unsupported identity MUST block contribution. One privately provisioned shared random secret MUST generate stable keyed response/turn receipts. A secret-domain mismatch or receipt-version change MUST block merge pending explicit migration. |
| A5 | Ordinary Git pushes MUST preserve unrelated pages/contributors. Stale parents MUST require fetch, remerge, regeneration and new exact-candidate review. Ambiguous transport MUST be resolved by remote identity readback before success. Failures MUST preserve the prior accepted publication. |
| A6 | Fresh independent semantic/privacy review MUST cover every outgoing contribution and complete combined tree, exact inputs and generic metadata. Same-agent, absent, stale or changed attestations MUST fail. Separate independent clone/readback MUST verify publication. |
| A7 | Rendered projections MUST contain only allowlisted aggregates and generic documentation. The transport ledger MAY additionally carry approved keyed receipts and strictly allowlisted numerical/model/phase/RTM facts. Receipts enable correlation and MUST NOT be described as anonymous. Unknown/missing/open/unmapped work and active tail MUST remain visible. Pricing MUST remain dated API estimates with separate currencies and current-list counterfactuals. |
| A8 | Synthetic acceptance MUST cover disjoint computers, retries/new observations/copied and conflicting overlap, simultaneous writers, stale parents, ambiguous pushes, unrelated-page preservation, map contention, unavailable inputs, invalid labels, symlinks/corrupt manifests, stale/same-agent review, supported private snapshot/map migration and failure preservation. Downloaded installed release MUST run the synthetic walkthrough without real history or tracker access. |

## Architecture and boundaries

The tracked core SHOULD live under `tools/usage`, separate from ignored legacy tooling. It MUST be a typed standard-library maintenance tool, with explicit strict schema validation at every JSON boundary; it is separate from the planned Pydantic/Typer catalog runtime. Git is the existing transport dependency. No daemon, billing integration, hosted service or new runtime package is required. Planning MUST define packaging that makes this core runnable from downloaded installable tooling artifacts without implementing catalog commands.

The pipeline MUST separate read-only local importer, private mapping/receipt conversion, validated contribution ledger, deterministic aggregate renderer, frozen candidate, independent review with bound execution evidence and ordinary-push/readback. An implementation MAY adapt the existing importer only after sanitizing code, defaults, documentation and fixtures. Actual source access MUST require explicit local configuration. Synthetic tests MUST use explicit disposable sources/remotes/state.

### Private identity and merge

Setup MUST create a random contributor ID in private persistent state, independent of machine names, and require an externally provisioned 256-bit shared secret. It MUST NOT provision or transport that secret over Git. Private permission-restricted files MUST hold secret, source selector, maps, candidate inputs and receipts-to-source associations. A domain marker MUST be HMAC-SHA256 of a fixed versioned domain string using the secret; raw secret digests MUST NOT be exported. Different markers MUST fail rather than create a second corpus.

Receipts MUST use HMAC-SHA256 over canonical JSON tuples with explicit version/type domain separation: response identity includes native stable thread and response identity; turn identity includes native stable thread and turn identity. Neither tuple may include checkout path, hostname, tokens or mutable attribution. Thread, root, and parent relationships needed for counts MAY use separately domain-separated keyed receipts, never original IDs. Missing/ambiguous stable source identity MUST quarantine records and block affected contribution; content-derived identities that change with observation MUST NOT be accepted as dedup proof.

The schema-v1 ledger MUST retain complete latest contributor observations, keyed by contributor ID and monotonic local generation with predecessor digest. An identical generation/digest is a no-op; differing content at the same generation, forks, rollback or lost contributor state MUST fail with recovery instructions. A new validated generation replaces that contributor's previous observation set, not a cumulative aggregate. Missing input MUST NOT generate an empty replacement. Preserved prior records and explicit removals MUST distinguish unavailable history from intentional correction; corrections MUST be reviewed.

Combined canonical records MUST be keyed by receipt across all latest contributions. Exact matching observations collapse. Unknown-to-known fact enrichment MAY merge only when non-null values agree; open-to-closed turn refinement MAY merge when known facts agree. Conflicting non-null token/model/timing or primary attribution values MUST quarantine the receipt and block the candidate, never silently prefer a contributor or count both. A later observation from one contributor MUST NOT overwrite contradictory evidence still supplied by another. Conflict diagnostics MUST expose counts and technical reasons, never raw identities. Private diagnostics MAY identify local records only in authorized private files.

### Allowlist and measurement semantics

Transport MUST reject unknown keys, arbitrary labels, nonfinite/negative numbers, booleans masquerading as integers, unsupported schema versions and inconsistent token subsets. Permitted facts comprise version/domain/generation framing, keyed relationship receipts, observation/event times needed for dated costs and interval unions, nonnegative token counters or null, bounded exact public model/provider/effort/tier enums or unknown, fixed phases, current public RTM IDs or shared/coordinator/unallocated, opaque registered task/feature labels, parent-known status, timing basis, and reviewed public rate provenance. Model/provider values MUST be configured from reviewed public vocabularies; free-form source settings MUST remain private/unknown. Contributor identifiers MUST be opaque. Arbitrary evidence strings, source hashes/paths, prompts, names and private attribution provenance MUST NOT enter transport.

Rendering MUST omit all receipts and contributor identifiers. Alternate requirement/task/feature/model views MUST reconcile to one response corpus; associated requirements MUST NOT duplicate primary allocation. Mapping precedence MUST remain response then turn then thread independently per dimension. Unsupported historical mappings MUST remain unallocated. Conflicting response-level categories MUST leave turn duration mixed/unallocated once.

Time MUST preserve recorded duration, explicitly counted derived fallback, summed closed intervals, global closed interval union, observation span, overlap/parallelism and open/missing counts as distinct facts. Timing includes source turns without responses; response-bearing turn counts use their own denominator. Model time and productive time remain unknown. Cross-computer unions MUST be recomputed from deduplicated intervals, never summed contributor wallclock. Category unions are nonadditive. Clock discrepancies MUST remain conflicts/limitations rather than fabricated precision.

Token metrics MUST retain known subtotals and missing counts; cached input is within input and reasoning within output. Decimal costs MUST subtract cached input before applying input rates, retain unpriced/invalid categories, separate currencies, apply event-date rates and independently compute measurement-date list-price counterfactuals. Unsupported cache writes, missing exact models/rates/tier constraints and unknown facts MUST remain unpriced. Actual bills MUST NOT be inferred. Measured-as-of and remotely confirmed publication time MUST remain separate; active tail and historical completeness remain unknown.

### Concurrency, review and failure

Private writes MUST use exclusive locks, temporary files, fsync where available and atomic replacement. A killed writer MUST leave previous pointers valid; lock recovery MUST require confirming the owner is inactive. Setup/read/write MUST reject symlinks, unsafe paths and corrupt manifests. Source file reads MUST use stable captured prefixes; SQLite MUST use read-only transactions. An observational snapshot MUST NOT claim cross-source transaction consistency. Limits on input bytes/records and diagnostic output MUST be explicit and tested. Parsers MUST NOT execute input content.

Candidate manifests MUST bind source/input digests, receipt domain/schema, contribution generations, remote parent, complete outgoing file-tree digests, generator invocation and generic author/message metadata. Review MUST cover all unchanged outgoing files as well as changed ones. Publication MUST recompute bindings immediately before commit/push; only owned ledger/projection paths MAY change. Preparation MUST stop with review-required status. Check MUST be read-only. Resume MUST use the frozen reviewed inputs, never refresh implicitly.

A reviewer-name CLI option or a bare PASS file MUST NOT establish independent review. The supported review operation MUST consume an exact-candidate attestation plus a separate fresh-execution evidence file supplied by the coordinator/reviewer workflow. Evidence MUST identify task, generator and reviewer invocation IDs, review scope, disposition and exact tree/input/metadata/parent bindings. The tool MUST reject identical invocation IDs, absent/mismatched bindings, stale evidence and an attestation lacking that evidence; it MUST NOT generate a passing review itself. The coordinator MUST establish from actual fresh-agent dispatch/return evidence that the reviewer invocation exists and is independent, retain that evidence privately, and provide the bound evidence file. The tool MUST validate its strict schema and freeze its digest before resume. This is a supported procedural trust boundary under the existing protocol, not cryptographic proof of reviewer identity: a process with full private-state access could forge files. Documentation MUST state that limitation and MUST NOT claim the validator authenticates semantic independence. Fresh independent review of the complete candidate remains mandatory on every computer; an alternate string alone never fulfills it. Synthetic tests MUST supply explicitly synthetic execution evidence only for disposable local remotes and MUST NOT reuse it for actual publication.

On stale parent, the tool MUST preserve the rejected candidate, fetch the accepted remote ledger, apply the pending contributor replacement, revalidate all overlap and regenerate from the new parent. A changed parent/tree/input/metadata MUST invalidate review. Ordinary push MUST never force or erase unrelated pages. An ambiguous push MUST query the remote commit and verify exact reviewed tree/ancestry before recording accepted status; uncertainty MUST remain pending, with retry/readback available. Only confirmed remote identity MAY update the local accepted pointer. Fresh independent clone/readback MUST validate ledger, projections and metadata after publication; local submit and remote verification MUST have separate statuses.

### Compatibility and migration

The command surface SHOULD retain `refresh`, `check`, `contribute` and `update` with explicit private source/state/configuration arguments. Planning MUST freeze exact options, schemas and exit codes before implementation. There is no public Python API commitment. Existing ignored snapshots/maps MUST remain usable by their old tool and MUST NOT be edited or automatically published by setup. An explicit private migration MUST support the existing schema-v1 snapshot bundle (manifest and hashed accounting outputs), phase-map entries, and schema-v1 reviewed attribution registry. It MUST validate supported layouts against synthetic compatibility fixtures, copy supported observations and explicit attribution into separate private state, and preserve every legacy input byte and old-tool pointer. Setup MUST NOT trigger migration. Repeated identical migration MUST be idempotent; failure or contention MUST leave both legacy and accepted new state unchanged.

Migration MUST preserve unknown/missing/open/unmapped distinctions, recorded attribution precedence and private evidence; inferred legacy labels MUST NOT become reviewed attribution. Unsupported versions, corrupt hashes, conflicting mapping dimensions, unsafe paths and ambiguous identity MUST fail with bounded generic diagnostics, never guess an allocation. Legacy truncated/derived identifiers MUST NOT establish receipt identity. Promotion to a receipt-backed contribution MUST require a unique privately supplied association verified against configured stable native source identities; unassociated observations MUST remain a private historical/nonadditive archive with explicit unknown corpus coverage. Missing histories MUST NOT erase preserved observations or produce an empty replacement. Private source identities, evidence, labels and associations MUST remain outside transport; only reviewed allowlisted facts MAY be promoted after identity validation. Migration MUST NOT transport secrets, auto-import private files into Git, refresh histories or publish anything.

Historical aggregate-only dashboards MUST NOT be summed with receipt-backed observations. Migration MUST either rebuild the complete intended corpus from available original histories under one receipt domain and review the replacement, or retain the legacy dashboard separately as historical/nonadditive and declare the new corpus boundary and incompleteness. Missing historical sources MUST remain unknown. Secret rotation/version changes MUST require explicit cross-domain dedup migration; until implemented they MUST fail closed.

The published wiki Usage-Refresh protocol still describes ignored single-computer tooling and a full identifier ban. This task MUST NOT update that published protocol or use the new ledger for actual contributions. Repository setup instructions MUST state that migration/publication remains excluded and needs a separately reviewed protocol transition before real use. Local synthetic end-to-end demonstrations do not establish tracker migration.

## Risk disposition and traceability

Agent architecture readiness, 2026-11-17: this design is ready for fresh planning, conditional on the exact-document QA/reconciliation required by [documentation QA](documentation-qa.md). This is agent readiness, not human architecture approval. No unresolved high-risk decision requires another human request. Stable receipt correlation is the explicit accepted requirements scope; it remains a moderate privacy risk. Compromised participating machines can expose the secret/raw histories, and a shared-secret ledger cannot authenticate measurement truth. Receipt HMACs provide correlation-resistant identity outside the trust group, not contributor honesty. Authenticated independent review and strict projection boundaries mitigate accidental disclosure; they do not make receipts anonymous. No actual histories, secrets or external publication are changed here, so the proposed maintenance implementation has bounded reversible effects.

| Supporting requirement | Acceptance/design mapping | Execution evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NFR-006 / CAP-05 | A1–A8; phase/review/ledger and task handoff | [Authoritative task stages](tasks/usage-tooling.md#stage-ledger) |
| NFR-007 / CAP-05 | A1–A8; synthetic acceptance and failure boundaries | [Authoritative task stages](tasks/usage-tooling.md#stage-ledger) |
| NFR-008 / CAP-04 | A1/A4/A6/A7/A8; private identity, allowlist and authenticated review | [Authoritative task stages](tasks/usage-tooling.md#stage-ledger) |

The [implementation plan](usage-tooling-plan.md) defines the ordered increments and verification contracts. The [task record](tasks/usage-tooling.md) owns exact source identity, current implementation/verification evidence, the stage ledger and next-phase routing.

purpose: Exact approved maintenance specification and agent-authorized plan evidence; repository originals remain authoritative.
